question.problem: Determine if ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14116680/assets/5da5dddce497b4b2b8ffe24924714e960a3c43088351e0a2a6d039000ed78035.svg) is an eigenvector of the matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14116680/assets/6a73978c951c4ae02d1455b5881a210c3d415bf1beef2f6f41f694c361708422.svg) If so, then what is the corresponding eigenvalue?
question.worked_solution:
The eigenvectors of $A$ are the non-zero vectors $\mathbf{v}$ such that $A\mathbf{v}=\lambda \mathbf{v}.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}Av & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =4\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =4v.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $A\mathbf{v}=4 \mathbf{v},$ we conclude that $\mathbf{v}$ is an eigenvector of $A$ and the corresponding eigenvalue is $\lambda=4.$
